questions.question: Name the four factors of production and the reward (remuneration) of each, with an example of each from a mobile coffee business.
questions.expected_answer: Natural resources (land) — rent: the trading spot, water, coffee beans from farms. Labour — wages and salaries: the barista. Capital — interest: the trailer, espresso machine, grinder and the money used to buy them. Entrepreneurship — profit: the owner who spots the opportunity, combines the factors and carries the risk; profit is the residual after paying rent, wages and interest and may be a loss.

questions.question: Distinguish between own capital and borrowed capital. Give three sources of each and two advantages and two disadvantages of each.
questions.expected_answer: Own capital: provided by the owner, not repaid, no interest — savings, contributions from family, retained profits, selling personal assets (shares for companies). Advantages: no repayment or interest; owner keeps full control; lowers risk and helps future borrowing. Disadvantages: limited amount; owner's savings at risk; opportunity cost. Borrowed capital: from outsiders, repaid with interest — bank loans, overdrafts, vehicle/equipment finance, trade credit, development agencies (SEFA, NEF). Advantages: larger amounts and faster growth; owner keeps ownership and profit after interest. Disadvantages: interest and instalments payable regardless of profit; collateral required and may be lost; strain on cash flow.

questions.question: An entrepreneur needs R100 000. She has R40 000 own capital and borrows R60 000 at 12% simple interest per year. Calculate the interest for one year and two years, the total repayable after one year, and the percentage financed by debt. Explain what gearing means.
questions.expected_answer: Interest for one year = 60 000 × 12% = R7 200; for two years = R14 400. Total repayable after one year = 60 000 + 7 200 = R67 200. Debt share = 60 000 ÷ 100 000 × 100 = 60%. Gearing is the proportion of borrowed capital to own capital; a highly geared business is financed mainly by debt, which increases both the potential reward and the risk because interest and repayments must be paid regardless of profit.
